newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria delays transfer of agencies funds to banks.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria delays transfer of agencies funds to banks.

text.p: Nigeria's military government has put on hold a key decision to transfer accounts of government agencies to commercial and merchant banks from the Central Bank, according to finance minister Anthony Ani.
He told the independent Thisday newspaper in an interview published on Monday that the government believed the time was not yet ripe to put too much money into circulation.
"Any decison to inject more money into the economy will adversely affect it," Ani said.
In January, the government announced as one of its key fiscal 1997 policies the transfer of accounts of its agencies to commercial banks to divest retail banking from the Central Bank.
Ani said indices such as interest and inflation rates showed it was not right to transfer the accounts at this time.
A 21 percent cap on interest rates was lifted last October and rates have since fallen to single digits partly because the system is awash with naira.
Tight spending based on the "guided deregulation" economic policy introduced by the government has reduced the inflation rate to below 30 percent from well over 70 percent in 1995.
Ani told Thisday that inflation was now at 23 percent but this trend could be jeorpadised if there was too much money in circulation.

"The PTF (Petroleum Trust Fund) has released some 29 billion naira into the system. I'm also going to release 44 billion naira from the capital budget this week... and all will affect the system we're trying to put right," he said.
The PTF was formed to use money from a 1994 hike in petrol for repairing the country's dilapidated public infrastructure.
